description: Store one JSON document in private temporary storage for repeated process_json queries; this does not run a jq filter. Use when the same input will be queried more than once. For a single query, pass input or url directly to process_json instead. Provide exactly one of input or url, never both. A local file must be sent to REST POST /uploads by the client; this tool cannot read local paths. Maximum 5 MiB; URLs must be public HTTPS JSON on port 443, without credentials, private addresses, or custom headers. URL fetching is bounded to three redirects and ten seconds. Returns success:true, a secret upload_id, expires_at (UTC), and size_bytes. The ID is reusable for 15 minutes; uploads do not refresh expiration when queried. Uploads are immutable: create a new upload to change the JSON, then delete the old ID. Anyone holding the ID can inspect, query, or delete it. Use get_upload for metadata, process_json for contents or filtering, and delete_upload for early cleanup. Consumes one shared daily quota call on the free tier; active prepaid passes bypass that counter. Retrying creates another upload. No signup; a UUID bearer header selects the access tier but does not establish upload ownership. Failures return success:false and error, with status 400 for invalid input/URL/JSON, 413 for oversize data, 415 for unsupported content, 502/504 for URL failures, or 503 for storage failure. Exhausted quota returns a tool error with remaining:0, reset_at, and a structured upgrade offer linking pricing and checkout; inspect _meta.rateLimit for limit and reset.

input.description: One JSON value to store, including null. Choose input or url, never both. Local files must first be uploaded through POST /uploads.

url.description: Public HTTPS JSON URL to fetch once and store, up to 5 MiB. Port 443 only; no credentials, private networks, or custom headers. Choose url or input, never both.

name: upload_json
title: Upload reusable JSON
